cards.explanation: The answer is all day long. Verse 97 says, "Oh, how I love Your law! All day long it is my meditation." Not a quick visit, friends, and not a drive-by. The whole day is his time with God's law.

The answer is that the commandments are always with him. Verse 98 says, "Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies, for they are always with me." The reason is that they stay with him, friends. He doesn't have to go looking for them when trouble shows up.

The answer is True. Verse 99 says, "I have more insight than all my teachers, for Your testimonies are my meditation." He gives the reason right in the verse, friends. His insight comes from thinking on God's testimonies.

The answer is obeys. Verse 100 says, "I discern more than the elders, for I obey Your precepts." Notice it's obeying, friends, not just knowing. He puts God's precepts into practice, and that's the reason he gives.

The answer is False. Verse 102 says, "I have not departed from Your ordinances, for You Yourself have taught me." The teacher is God, not the elders. The psalmist stays put, friends, because of what God taught him.

The answer is sweeter than honey. Verse 103 says God's words are sweeter than honey in his mouth. Honey is about as sweet as it gets, friends, and he says God's words beat it. I'm just saying, it's a tough standard for any cookie.

The answer is false. Verse 104 says, "I gain understanding from Your precepts; therefore I hate every false way." Notice the "therefore," bakers. The understanding comes first, and the hatred of false ways follows from it.

The answer is that it shows him where to step. Verse 105 says, "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path." A lamp for your feet is about seeing where you're walking. Anybody who's crossed a dark room knows how much a little light helps, friends.

The answer is word. Verse 107 says, "I am severely afflicted, O LORD; revive me through Your word." He's hurting badly, friends, and he turns to the LORD's word to be revived. I think that says a lot about where he goes when things get heavy.

The answer is that he asks the LORD to teach him His judgments. Verse 108 says, "Accept the freewill offerings of my mouth, O LORD, and teach me Your judgments." He brings the offerings of his mouth and then asks to keep learning. Even a man who's already wise wants more lessons, friends.

The answer is law. Verse 109 says, "I constantly take my life in my hands, yet I do not forget Your law." His life is on the line, friends, and God's law still stays in his mind. That's some serious holding on.

The answer is True. Verse 110 says, "The wicked have set a snare for me, but I have not strayed from Your precepts." A trap is set, friends, and he stays on God's path anyway. That's one careful walker.

The answer is that they are the joy of his heart. Verse 111 says, "Your testimonies are my heritage forever, for they are the joy of my heart." Heritage and joy go together here, friends. What he's been given is something he's glad to hold.

The answer is False. Verse 112 says, "I have inclined my heart to perform Your statutes, even to the very end." The verse doesn't tie it to his troubles ending, friends. He says he has inclined his heart to perform them to the very end.
The answer is that they keep someone safe. Verse 114 says, "You are my hiding place and my shield…" A hiding place and a shield are both about safety, friends. Two pictures, one message.

The answer is False. Verse 114 says, "You are my hiding place and my shield; I put my hope in Your word." The verse names what he puts his hope in, friends, and it's God's word. His own strength isn't mentioned.

The answer is so he can obey God's commandments. Verse 115 says, "Depart from me, you evildoers, that I may obey the commandments of my God." He's clearing space so he can obey, friends. Sometimes you've got to say it out loud.

The answer is hope. Verse 116 says, "Sustain me as You promised, that I may live; let me not be ashamed of my hope." He's asking the LORD to hold him up, friends, and he ties that request to what God promised. The thing he doesn't want to be ashamed of is his hope.

The answer is that he will be saved. Verse 117 says, "Uphold me, and I will be saved, that I may always regard Your statutes." He asks to be upheld and says he will be saved, friends. He also says why: so he can always regard God's statutes.

The answer is True. Verse 118 says, "You reject all who stray from Your statutes, for their deceitfulness is in vain." Their deceitfulness doesn't get them anywhere, friends. The psalmist says it plainly.

The answer is that he loves God's testimonies. Verse 119 says, "All the wicked on earth You discard like dross; therefore I love Your testimonies." He ends up loving God's testimonies, friends. His response is love, not a shrug.
The answer is awe. Verse 120 says, "My flesh trembles in awe of You; I stand in fear of Your judgments." That's a big, whole-body kind of awe, friends. Even his knees are paying attention.
